The exact signed distance $d$ is computed by projecting the point onto the plane of the torus's major ring and measuring the distance to the minor ring's center [S1, S6, unofficial][S7].

The claim states that the signed distance is computed by projecting the point onto the plane of the torus's major ring and measuring the distance to the minor ring's center. Source [S1] provides the formula $q = (p_x^2 + p_z^2)^{1/2} - r_1, p_y)$ and $d = ||q|| - r_2$. This formula effectively calculates the distance from the point $(p_x, p_y, p_z)$ to the circle in the XZ-plane (the plane of the major ring) with radius $r_1$, and then subtracts the minor radius $r_2$. Specifically, the term $( (p_x^2 + p_z^2)^{1/2} - r_1, p_y )$ represents the 2D vector from the center of the minor ring (which lies on the major ring) to the projected point in the cross-sectional plane. Source [S6] confirms this logic with `float2 q = float2(length(p.xz) - t.x, p.y); return length(q) - t.y;`. Source [S7] describes the torus distance as a nested operation involving the major radius R and minor radius r, consistent with the geometric interpretation of projecting to the major ring's plane and measuring distance to the minor ring's center. Thus, the evidence supports the claim.
